Hardin County by the numbers

Where is the Hardin County Clerk, and what does the office hold for a home seller?

The clerk works from Suite 103 of the Hardin County Government Building, 150 N. Provident Way, Elizabethtown, KY 42701, and answers at 270-765-2171. Doors are open weekdays from 7:45 in the morning until 4:30 in the afternoon. A branch at 101 W. Lincoln Trail Blvd in Radcliff takes vehicle registrations Tuesday through Thursday from 8 to 4, but deeds go to Elizabethtown.

This is the county's keeper of deeds, mortgages, wills, plats, liens, assumed names and marriage records, and it also issues vehicle titles and tags and runs elections. A seller meets the office three ways: when the deed to the buyer is recorded, when an old mortgage needs a release of record, and when a bill that missed the sheriff's April 15 cutoff has moved to the clerk.

Courthouse fires in 1864 and 1932 destroyed county records, so a title examiner working on a very old chain may find gaps that predate the present 1934 courthouse.

Can I search Hardin County land records online?

Yes. The clerk's website runs an eSearch name search that works as a guest, and it indexes far more than deeds. The index types include deeds, mortgages, deeds of release, affidavits of descent, plats, powers of attorney, restrictions, wills, lis pendens, mechanics liens and ad valorem liens, along with fiscal court minutes and ordinances.

For a seller, two searches pay off before listing. A search on your own name should show the mortgage and, once paid, a deed of release. A search for liens should show nothing left unreleased, since a lien filed against a prior owner or a contractor can surface at a title company in the final week.

What does Kentucky require in a deed the Hardin County Clerk will accept?

The clerk records deeds for property in Hardin County, and it must turn away a deed that breaks a content rule in KRS 382.135 or KRS 382.110. Title attorneys cover these items routinely. A family transfer written from a form is where gaps show up.

  • Full names and mailing addresses for both parties.
  • The full price, backed by a notarized certificate signed by both sides. A gift deed carries a certificate saying so, with an estimated fair cash value.
  • An in care of address for the bill of the year of transfer.
  • The source of the grantor's title, by deed book and page when it came from a recorded deed, or a plain explanation when it came by inheritance.

An estate that passes land by will or intestacy adds one more filing: the personal representative lodges an affidavit listing who received each parcel and what it was valued at.

Which recording charges does the Hardin County Clerk list?

The clerk posts a fee schedule alongside its formatting rules. Paper should be white and unbound, black ink, no seals or highlighter, with a three inch blank strip across the top of page one. Electronic filers use Simplifile, ePn or CSC.

Sample Hardin County Clerk recording charges
DocumentCharge

Mortgage$80.00
Release of mortgage, full or partial$46.00
Affidavit of descent and distribution$50.00
Power of attorney$50.00

Will$47.00
Certified copy$5.00

Most documents add $3.00 for every page past five and $4.00 per extra reference, and a mortgage adds $3.00 per page past thirty. Confirm the total with the clerk before mailing a packet.

How much transfer tax does the seller owe at the Hardin County Clerk?

The grantor pays fifty cents per $500 block of value, with any leftover amount counted as a full block, under KRS 142.050. The clerk computes it from the value stated in the deed, collects before accepting the paper, and certifies the payment date and amount on the deed itself. The tax is collected once per transaction, in whichever county the deed is filed. The clerk keeps 5 percent for the work, and the rest goes to the county treasurer every three months for the general fund. On a $300,000 sale that is 600 blocks, or $300. On a house priced at the Census median value of $225,800 it is 452 blocks, or $226.

Foreclosure deeds, deeds in lieu, transfers between spouses in a divorce, partitions, and parent to child gifts with only nominal consideration are among the exemptions. When a deed carries no stated price, the tax is figured on the open market estimate.

What happens when the clerk rejects a deed or a deed arrives late?

The statute bars the clerk from lodging a deed that fails the content rules, so a rejected package usually means a corrected deed, a new notarization and a second trip. A deed recorded in error still counts as notice to later buyers and creditors, but the defect can still draw questions from a title insurer.

Timing rules apply to some transfers. A lender that takes a deed in lieu of foreclosure must file it with the clerk within 45 days of signing. A grantee under a deed from a court appointed commissioner has five business days from receipt to file. If you are the seller on either kind of transfer, confirm with the other side that the deed has been filed before you consider the matter closed.

Which other recordings might a Hardin County seller need?

Selling often trips over small filings. These come up most often, with the clerk's charges.

  • Release of a paid mortgage: $46.00.
  • Affidavit of descent and distribution after an inheritance: $50.00.
  • Power of attorney: $50.00, and a revocation: $46.00.
  • Release of a mechanics lien: $46.00, or $60.00 for a bond that releases it.
  • Release of a judgment lien or federal tax lien: $46.00. A state tax lien release costs $5.00.
  • City lien and city release: $23.00.
  • Notary service at the counter: $5.00 per acknowledgement plus $2.00 per notarization.

None of these replaces a title search, but ordering them early prevents the delay of a lender waiting on a release.

Where does the clerk fit into unpaid property tax in Hardin County?

The sheriff's page sends sellers to the clerk for payoff on any delinquent bill from a prior year. After April 15 a bill is a certificate of delinquency in the clerk's office, and the clerk's page offers a delinquent tax calculator and tax sale information. The recording schedule also lists $30.00 to record a certificate assignment and $46.00 for a reassignment or release.

Request a payoff in writing, dated near the closing date, because interest accrues monthly. If a third party bought the certificate, the payoff goes to that buyer.

What do Census figures say about the people who buy and sell in Hardin County?

The Census Bureau counts 44,622 households with 2.44 people each, and 84.6 percent of residents had not moved in the past year. Median gross rent is $971, per capita income $37,638, and 12,344 residents are veterans.

With Fort Knox in the county, some sellers and buyers work to a fixed report date. A deed that meets every content rule on the first attempt avoids a trip back to Suite 103.

More questions about Hardin County, KY County Clerk

Can a deed be e-recorded in Hardin County, Kentucky?

Yes. The Hardin County Clerk lists Simplifile, ePn and CSC as accepted electronic recording vendors.

How much is a mortgage release at the Hardin County Clerk?

$46.00 for a full or partial release, plus $3.00 for each page past five. The deed itself is $50.00.

How much is transfer tax on a $300,000 Hardin County sale?

$300. The rate is $0.50 per $500 of value, so 600 blocks of $500 times fifty cents, paid by the seller when the deed is filed.

Does the Radcliff branch record deeds?

No. The Radcliff branch at 101 W. Lincoln Trail Blvd handles vehicle registration on Tuesday through Thursday. Deeds are recorded at Suite 103, 150 N. Provident Way, Elizabethtown.

Is a state tax lien release cheaper than a federal one in Hardin County?

Yes. The clerk charges $5.00 to record a state tax lien or its release and $46.00 for a federal tax lien or release.

Boyd County by the numbers

Where do you record a deed in Boyd County, Kentucky?

You record it with the Boyd County Clerk. The main office sits at 2800 Louisa Street in Catlettsburg. The county also lists two Ashland-area branches, which spares sellers on that side of the county the drive to the seat.

  • Main office, 2800 Louisa Street, Catlettsburg, 606-739-5116, weekdays 8:30 a.m. to 4 p.m.

  • Cannonsburg office, 1315 Cannonsburg Road, 606-929-9595, weekdays 9 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.

The county page says holidays may change those hours. It also says the clerk records land records, wills, liens and lien releases, along with articles of incorporation and veterans discharges. Call the branch before you drive if you are bringing a deed that needs a notary.

What is Boyd County like for a seller?

Boyd County is a small, dense county on the Ohio River at the northeastern edge of Kentucky, about 160 square miles of land. Ashland is the largest city, Catlettsburg is the seat, and the county sits in the Huntington-Ashland metro area. The Census Bureau counts 301.9 people per square mile, far more crowded than a typical Bluegrass county.

Steel, refining and activated carbon have been the big employers, and the county's population has slid from about 55,500 in 1980 to an estimated 47,751 in 2025. Boyd County Public Schools, Ashland Independent and Fairview Independent each cover part of the county, and buyers usually ask which one serves your street.

What does the Boyd County Clerk charge to record?

On the clerk's fee schedule dated January 1, 2020, a deed is $50 and a mortgage is $80. Added pages and added parcel references raise the total, so phone 606-739-5116 for the current figure.

Selected Boyd County Clerk recording fees (clerk fee schedule effective January 1, 2020)

Page charges kick in after page five for most documents, at $3.00 each. Extra references cost $4.00 apiece on some items, and a mortgage carries the page charge only after page thirty.

How is the transfer tax figured in Boyd County?

The bottom of Boyd's schedule prints the transfer tax as a dollar per thousand dollars of value. The person selling pays it, and the clerk takes payment when the deed is handed over.

The Census Bureau's five-year survey puts a typical owner-occupied Boyd County home at $130,700. A sale there comes to 262 steps of $500, or $131.00 in tax. A $90,000 sale comes to $90.00. With prices this low, the tax is usually a smaller line on the settlement statement than the title charges.

Foreclosure transfers, spousal transfers and token-price deeds within a family can be exempt. If you are unsure about yours, ask the clerk before you sign, because a deed cannot be accepted until the right amount is paid.

What has to be in a deed before the clerk will accept it?

KRS 382.135 spells out what a Kentucky deed must carry: both parties' full names and mailing addresses, the whole price, and an address for the current year's tax bill.

  • For a sale, both sides sign a notarized oath that the price in the deed is what was paid.
  • For a gift, the oath says so and adds an estimated fair cash value.
  • The deed points back to the earlier recorded deed or other source of the seller's title.
  • A deed that fails these tests is refused at the counter.

The grantor's recorded source of title is the item most often missing from do-it-yourself deeds. If your deed came from a family member years ago and was never recorded, tell your closing attorney early, since a gap there can hold up a cash closing.

How do inherited Boyd County homes get recorded?

The executor or administrator swears out an affidavit naming each person who receives property and its value, and files it with the clerk. Boyd's schedule prices that affidavit at $50 and a recorded will at $47.

Estates can sit for months with a house unlisted and utilities running. A buyer who pays cash still needs the record to show who owned the property and who received it. Start with the affidavit, then ask the clerk or an attorney which other papers the county needs.

What does a Boyd County closing look like at the clerk's counter?

A closing attorney or title agent normally carries in the signed deed, the notarized price certificate and a check covering recording and transfer tax. Staff compare the deed to the state's content rules, collect the tax, note the date and amount on the deed and file it.

Plan for a few small costs on top of the deed fee. A release of an existing mortgage lists at $46, and a mortgage payoff means a second recording after closing. For a $130,000 Catlettsburg sale you might see $50 for the deed, $46 for one release and $130.00 in transfer tax, which comes to $226 before page charges. Your closing agent will give you the real totals.

The county courthouse in Catlettsburg dates from 1912, replacing the first one built in 1861. Ashland is the larger city, so many sellers there use the Carter Avenue office and skip the drive to the seat.

Who handles delinquent property taxes in Boyd County?

The Boyd County Clerk's office takes over delinquent taxes from prior years. The county's tax page sends payers to 606-739-5116, option 4.

The Sheriff's Office collects the current year's bill. That split means an old unpaid bill is a clerk question and this year's bill is a sheriff question. A closing agent will check both before a sale funds, and a seller who knows of a delinquent bill should ask the clerk for the payoff amount.

Do older Boyd County deeds sit in other counties' books?

Possibly. Boyd County was formed in 1860 from parts of Greenup, Carter and Lawrence Counties, so a chain of title that reaches back before that date can lead into the records of those older counties. Title examiners follow the chain wherever it goes.

If your family has held the land since the nineteenth century, tell the closing attorney early. A call to the Boyd clerk's main office will show how far back the county's own indexes run.

How tight is the Boyd County housing market?

Owners occupy 70.2% of homes here, typical rent is $849 a month and the typical household earns $61,118. The Census Bureau counts 18.0% of residents in poverty, and the average trip to work takes 22.1 minutes. About 21,818 housing units stood in the county in 2025, and just 12 building permits were issued that year.

With so few new homes going up, sellers here compete mostly with other resale houses. A clean title and a complete deed package are the part you control.

More questions about Boyd County, KY County Clerk

How do I contact the Boyd County Clerk?

Call 606-739-5116 for the main office at 2800 Louisa Street in Catlettsburg. The Ashland office is 606-325-3547 and the Cannonsburg office is 606-929-9595.

How much does a deed cost to record in Boyd County?

Fifty dollars on the schedule dated January 1, 2020, with $3 added for each page after the fifth. Call to confirm the amount before you mail anything.

What is the transfer tax in Boyd County?

One dollar per thousand dollars of value, printed at the foot of the clerk's schedule. The seller pays it.

Can I record in the Ashland office instead of Catlettsburg?

Possibly. The county lists Ashland and Cannonsburg offices under the County Clerk, but the page does not say which document types each branch accepts. Call the branch first to confirm it will take your deed.

Where do I pay delinquent Boyd County property taxes from a prior year?

Through the clerk's phone line at 606-739-5116, option 4. This year's bill goes to the sheriff instead.

Jessamine County by the numbers

Where is a Jessamine County deed recorded?

Deeds for Jessamine County land go to the county clerk's recording desk at the Nicholasville courthouse, 101 North Main Street. The office is staffed on weekdays from 8 until 4, and the number to call is (859) 885-4161.

A second counter operates in Wilmore at 210 South Lexington Avenue, weekdays from 9 until 3. The county's listing does not break down which services that branch handles, so ask before you carry a closing package there. Nicholasville is the seat and the largest city, which is why most sellers simply use the courthouse.

A house sale usually leaves three papers for the clerk: the deed to the buyer, the lender's payoff release, and sometimes an affidavit. The buyer's title agent expects all of them indexed before funds are released.

Bring these to the counter:

  • The signed, notarized deed with the sale price stated, because the deed tax is figured from that number.
  • A check for the recording charge and the tax. KRS 64.012 also lists a $5 charge when the clerk notarizes the deed on the spot.
  • The lender's release, if it has not been filed. The posted minimum for a release is $46.

The county's clerk page also carries an open records request form for anyone who needs copies later.

What does the Jessamine County Clerk charge to record a deed?

On the clerk's fee page a deed starts at $50 and a mortgage at $80. That page is dated to 2020, so phone ahead for the current total before writing a check.

Source: Jessamine County Clerk, Standard Recording Fees.

Documents past five pages add $3 per extra page, and a mortgage adds the same amount after page thirty. The state's base figure in KRS 64.012 is $33 for up to five pages, so the clerk's totals clearly stack other charges on top. Treat any posted number as a starting point.

How much deed transfer tax does a Jessamine County seller owe?

The seller pays 50 cents for every $500 of price stated in the deed, with any leftover amount rounded up to a full $500 block. The clerk collects it at the counter, and a deed is not accepted for recording until it is paid.

To see how it works, take the county's Census median home value of $268,100. That is 536 full blocks plus a remainder, so 537 blocks at 50 cents gives $268.50. A $400,000 sale produces $400.00. Only one county collects the tax on a sale, the one holding the land.

KRS 142.050 excuses a long list of transfers. A few matter to ordinary households:

  • Husband and wife swaps, and transfers between ex-spouses as part of a divorce.
  • Parent to child, or grandparent to grandchild, with only token payment.
  • A corrective deed that fixes one already of record.
  • A foreclosure, or a surrender of the home to the lender in lieu of one.
  • A deed that only pledges or frees property as security for a loan.

If a deed is a gift and no exemption fits, the clerk uses the likely open-market price instead.

Can I search or e-record Jessamine County land records online?

Yes, with a subscription. The clerk runs eCCLIX for viewing and printing indexed documents, and four vendors are listed for electronic recording. Inside the office, the same records can be viewed at no charge.

According to the clerk, deeds, mortgages and wills are indexed from June 30, 1966, scanned images online cover most filings since January 2004, and marriage entries start in 1798. For an old boundary question or a decades-old lien, start with the in-office index.

  • eCCLIX: login issued by the site administrator, with charges for data and images.
  • Indecomm: (704) 412-3179.
  • CSC: (866) 652-0111.
  • Simplifile: (800) 460-5657.
  • ePN: (888) 325-3365.

Another tool is DOCALERT, a free email notice that fires whenever a deed or mortgage is filed under a name you register. People who own inherited or empty parcels in the county get the most from it, because a bogus filing is simpler to challenge when caught within days.

What happens to the tax bill once the deed is on record?

The county Property Valuation Administrator picks up the transfer and changes the owner of record. The sheriff, not the clerk, sends the bill, and the clerk returns to the picture only if a bill stays unpaid.

The PVA notes that the age 65 homestead exemption is attached to the owner, not the parcel. Anyone who sells should tell the office so the credit leaves the old address. The PVA posted $49,100 as the exemption for 2025 to 2026.

Unpaid bills pass to the clerk after April 15, and the clerk's website carries a delinquent tax search. State revenue officials say 1 percent monthly interest and commissions begin at that point. A seller with an old unpaid bill should settle it before signing the deed, and the clerk can quote the payoff.

What else does the Jessamine County Clerk's office handle for a home seller?

The same clerk who records the deed also runs several services a seller touches around a move. The county government lists deeds and mortgages, delinquent taxes, notary commissions, voter registration and vehicle registration among its clerk services.

  • Voter registration: a change of address after the sale goes through the clerk's election department.
  • Vehicle registration renewals: the clerk's site offers a renewal tool that asks for a title number, a plate number and a card.
  • Delinquent tax lookups: the clerk's site links to a search, and the clerk alone sets the dollar amount owed at the time of payment.
  • Land records: eCCLIX covers last-minute title follow-ups, estate settlements and appraisals.

Estate sellers should note that wills and affidavits of descent are recorded at the same counter, at the $47 and $50 starting charges on the fee page. An heir listing an inherited house in Jessamine County should ask the clerk which of those papers the title company will want on record.

What does the Jessamine County housing base look like?

The county gained roughly 4,000 residents between the 2020 count of 52,991 and a July 2025 estimate of 57,147, a rise of 7.8 percent. Census figures list 22,061 housing units and 512 building permits in 2025.

Jessamine was split off from Fayette County in December 1798, and the clerk says some of its records date to the 1700s. Today the county belongs to the Lexington-Fayette metro area. Its whole southern edge follows the Kentucky River, about 172 square miles of land lie inside its borders, and Nicholasville and Wilmore are its two cities, with High Bridge a census-designated place.

Two thirds of homes, 66.7 percent, are lived in by their owners, and households earn a median of $74,576. New subdivisions and former farm tracts keep the clerk's counter busy with plats, easements and survey references, each recorded as its own item with its own fee.

More questions about Jessamine County, KY County Clerk

Which office records a deed for a Jessamine County house?

The Jessamine County Clerk. Go to the courthouse at 101 North Main Street in Nicholasville or call (859) 885-4161.

Why is the clerk's recording charge higher than the state fee?

Which counter takes deeds for Daviess County property?

Deeds for Daviess County property are recorded at the Daviess County Clerk's legal recording department, Room 104 at 212 St. Ann Street in Owensboro. The window opens at 8 in the morning and closes at 4:30, and the recording phone line is 270-685-8434, option 3. Mail goes to the same street address, ZIP code 42303.

How can I pay the Daviess County Clerk for recording?

The office takes several forms of payment, with one limit on personal checks. Pick the method before you send a deed through the mail so the package is not returned.

  • Cash, cashier's check, certified check, business check or money order
  • Credit or debit card, with a vendor fee added
  • Personal checks only from in-state addresses with all information pre-printed
  • No counter checks

Daviess County follows the formatting standards that the Kentucky County Clerks' Association adopted from the Property Records Industry Association. A deed that breaks them can be turned away at the counter, which delays your closing.

Daviess County document format rules (source: Daviess County Clerk, PRIA Standards page)
ItemRequirement
Paper20 lb. white, no watermarks, 8.5 x 11 preferred, 8.5 x 14 accepted
PrintOne side only, black ink preferred, dark blue signatures, 10-point Times New Roman or similar
Margins1 inch all around, with the top 3 inches of page one left blank for the recorder
Not allowedStaples or binding, impression seals, colored highlighter

Under KRS 142.050 the seller owes $0.50 on every $500 slice of the price, and a partial slice counts as a whole one. The clerk calculates the amount from the value written in the deed and collects before accepting it. A deed at the typical Daviess County home value of $199,900 covers 400 slices, so the tax is $200.

The clerk keeps 5 percent of what it collects and sends the rest to the county treasurer. Several transfers are exempt, including:

  • Deeds that only confirm or correct an earlier deed
  • Transfers between spouses, or former spouses in a divorce
  • Foreclosure deeds and deeds in lieu of foreclosure
  • Transfers to or from a government body
  • Parent to child or grandparent to grandchild for nominal consideration

How do I get copies of recorded Daviess County documents?

Land records are public, except military discharge papers. You can walk in during office hours or mail a written request with payment, a return address and a phone number. Allow up to three business days for a mailed request. Staff will fetch a document you identify but will not research for you.

Walk-in copies cost $0.50 a page, or $1.00 for 11 x 17 paper. A certified copy is $5.00 for the first three pages and $0.50 for each additional page. Mail and fax requests cost $1.00 a page, and a certified copy by mail is $5.00 for three pages plus $1.00 for each extra page. Certified copies are not available by fax.

Can I search Daviess County land records online?

The clerk has digitized deeds, mortgages, plats and wills back to 1974 and announced a goal of reaching records to June 30, 1966 by June 2026. Questions about the service go to the legal recording department at 270-685-8434, extension 3.

A title company will normally pull the chain of title for you, but a seller can use the same index to check that the last deed, any mortgage release and any easements are on file before listing the house.

What else does the Daviess County Clerk handle for property owners?

Two property-tax jobs land on the clerk's desk even though the sheriff bills the tax. First, the clerk receives assessment appeals. After a conference with the PVA, an owner files the appeal with the clerk before the office closes on the next workday after the May inspection period ends. The clerk also serves as clerk of the local board of assessment appeals and notifies the owner of the hearing date.

Second, unpaid bills arrive in the clerk's office after April 25 as certificates of delinquency. A 10 percent clerk fee is added, along with interest and a county attorney fee. From mid-July the clerk can sell the certificates, and the list must be published a month or more ahead of a sale. A seller with a delinquency should call 270-685-8434 for the payoff.

Which Daviess County phone numbers are worth saving before closing?

  • County Clerk, recording and copies: 270-685-8434, option 3
  • Sheriff's tax counter, current bill and payoff: 270-685-6133
  • PVA, assessment, exemptions and ownership records: 270-685-8474
  • City of Owensboro Tax Office, city tax: 270-687-8537

The sheriff's office points anyone with questions about assessments, appeals, tax rates and bill collection to the PVA and the clerk, so those two offices are the right place to start when a number on a bill looks wrong.

What should a Daviess County seller check before the deed is signed?

Gather the paperwork so the recording is clean on the first try. A few checks save a return trip to Room 104.

  • Confirm that every prior mortgage has a recorded release.
  • Match the grantor names on the deed to the names on the last recorded deed.
  • Print on white 8.5 x 11 paper, one side, with the top margin left empty.
  • State the full price in the deed so the clerk can compute transfer tax.
  • Ask the sheriff's tax office at 270-685-6133 for the current bill, since Daviess County property tax for the year is collected there and not at the clerk.

What does Daviess County look like for a house seller?

Daviess County, formed in 1815 from part of Ohio County, covers 477 square miles on the Ohio River with Owensboro as the seat. The Census Bureau counted 103,312 residents in 2020, and QuickFacts shows 45,155 housing units, 68.1 percent owner-occupancy, homes that typically value $199,900, and typical rent of $918.

The county also issued 253 building permits in 2025, so new construction adds to the pool of recorded transfers each year.

Call 270-685-8434 and choose option 3 for document recording. The legal recording department is in Room 104 at 212 St. Ann Street in Owensboro.

In person it is $5.00 for the first three pages and $0.50 for each additional page. By mail the extra pages cost $1.00 each.

Does the clerk handle property tax payments in Daviess County?

Which party owes the Kentucky deed tax in a Daviess County sale?

The seller, who is the grantor on the deed. Each $500 slice of price, partial ones included, costs $0.50, so a $199,900 deed carries $200.

Doors are open Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday and Friday from 7:30 until 4:30, and Thursday and Saturday mornings until noon.

Owners who disagree with a value must have a conference with the PVA during the May inspection period, then file with the clerk by the next workday after it closes. A city may adopt the county's annual assessment for property inside its limits, though vehicle taxes use a separate state-supervised assessment. In Edmonson County that point concerns Brownsville alone.

What else does the Edmonson County Clerk's office do besides deeds?

The same counter serves drivers and voters. The clerk's site links to vehicle registration renewal, driver license renewal through Drive.ky.gov, voter registration, a lookup of vehicle tax paid last year by VIN, and bridge toll payments through River Link. Two of those matter to a seller: the Find and View Delinquent Taxes page and the Find and View Land Records page, which opens the eCCLIX search.

Call 270-597-2624 before you go, since Thursday and Saturday close at noon and Friday stays open until 5.

What is Edmonson County like for a seller?

Who records a deed in Bourbon County, Kentucky?

The Bourbon County Clerk records it, in the county building at 301 Main Street, Room 106, in Paris. A house on a Paris street and a horse farm near Millersburg are recorded at the same counter.

The county directory shows the office open weekdays from half past eight until four-thirty, with a Thursday close at six in the evening. Call (859) 987-2142, extension 236. The county directory puts the Property Valuation Administrator down the hall in Room 15 and the sheriff, who collects tax bills, in Room 104. That short hallway matters when you sell: the deed, the assessment record and the tax bill all live within a few doors of each other.

What does Bourbon County sit on, and why does that matter for a deed?

Bourbon County covers about 290 square miles of gently rolling farmland in the Lexington area, with Paris as the seat and Millersburg and North Middletown as the other incorporated towns. It is one of Kentucky's nine original counties, formed in 1785.

Records here have a rough history. Fire destroyed the courthouse in 1872 and again in 1901, and records went with it. That history is one reason a seller should read the chain of title before signing a contract. The clerk's land records are where the buyer's title examiner reads that chain, and an old gap in a legal description can slow a closing.

  • Farm parcels can carry several tax parcels, and each extra reference adds $4.00 on the clerk's schedule.
  • Easements, leases and plats are recorded documents too, and each has its own line on the fee schedule.
  • The title search happens before closing, so recording problems tend to surface early.

What are the recording fees at the Bourbon County Clerk?

Length changes the bill. Past page five, most documents cost $3.00 more per page, and each added parcel reference is $4.00. A farm deed with several parcels costs more than a short town lot deed.

How much is the transfer tax on a Bourbon County sale?

Kentucky taxes the seller at the equivalent of $1 per $1,000 of price, rounded up in $500 steps. The clerk takes the money at the counter, and the deed is not accepted until it is paid.

The Census Bureau's five-year survey puts the typical owner-occupied Bourbon County home at $229,300. A sale at that figure runs to 459 half-thousand steps, so the seller owes $229.50. A $150,000 sale owes $150.00. The tax follows the value written in the deed, and for a sale that value includes any loan balances secured against the property.

Several transfers owe nothing. These come up most often:

  • Transfers made through foreclosure, or by handing the property to the lender instead.
  • Moves between spouses, including ex-spouses under a divorce.
  • Deeds from a parent to a child, or a grandparent to a grandchild, for token consideration.
  • Corrective deeds that fix an earlier recording.

What must a deed contain before the Bourbon County Clerk will file it?

The clerk cannot file a deed that leaves out the items Kentucky requires. Four things must appear on its face: who is selling, who is buying, a mailing address for each, and what was paid. A fifth item, a tax-bill address for the year of transfer, completes the list.

A sale also needs a notarized, sworn statement from both parties or their agents confirming that the price shown is the whole price. A gift needs a matching statement saying so, with an estimated fair cash value. The deed must also trace the seller's ownership, either by book and page of the earlier recorded deed or by explaining that the seller inherited. Most sellers leave the drafting to the title company or a Kentucky attorney.

What if the Bourbon County house came through an estate?

Before an estate is closed, the executor or administrator files a sworn list with the clerk showing who receives each property and what it is worth. The clerk's schedule prices an affidavit of descent at $50.

This step often decides whether an inherited Paris house can sell quickly. A buyer's title company wants the chain from the deceased owner to the heirs in the Bourbon County records before it will insure a purchase. If the estate has not filed, start there, and ask the clerk's office which documents your situation needs.

What liens and notices does the clerk record against a Bourbon County property?

The clerk's website walks through the kinds of claims filed in this office, and any of them can turn up in a title search: mechanics liens, judgment liens, lis pendens notices, tax liens and child support liens.

  • A judgment lien needs the court, case number and amount, and the clerk's page says the creditor or attorney signs it.
  • A lis pendens warns that title is in litigation and must name the court and action number.
  • A mechanics lien needs a notarized statement of the amount due and a property description specific enough to identify the parcel.
  • Each lien has its own release document, which is also recorded for a fee.

If you know of a lien, get a payoff letter from the holder and ask for a release you can record, so the closing agent can settle it from your proceeds.

Which other Bourbon County offices does a seller visit?

Most of them are close together. The county directory lists the PVA in Room 15, the sheriff in Room 104 and the treasurer in Room 210 of 301 Main Street, all on the same weekday schedule. Planning and code enforcement, which handle permits, zoning approvals and ordinance complaints, are at 525 High Street, and their number is (859) 987-2150.

A seller with an unpermitted porch or a code complaint on a Paris rental should call that High Street office before listing, since an open violation can surface during a buyer's inspection.

How does Bourbon County's housing profile affect a sale?

Bourbon County had an estimated 20,243 residents in 2025 and about 9,399 housing units. Owners live in 63.7% of Bourbon homes, the typical monthly rent is $822 and the typical household takes in $61,354, all from the Census Bureau's latest five-year survey. The average commute is 25.4 minutes.

A house with a tenant, a repair list or a stalled estate records the same way as any other. The deed, the transfer tax and any releases are the parts a seller controls.

Who records deeds in Fayette County, Kentucky?

The Fayette County Clerk's Land Records department does. It sits in Room 132 at 162 East Main Street in Lexington, and the number to call is 859-253-3344. Weekday copy and inquiry service runs until 4:30 in the afternoon, but recording stops at 4:00, so a closing package that arrives at 4:15 waits for the next business day.

The clerk's is a constitutional office whose duties come from the Kentucky Revised Statutes. Besides recording, it prepares property tax bills, runs elections and titles vehicles. Fayette was one of the three original counties created in 1780, and its land records reach back to about 1792, the year Kentucky became a state. They exist in books, on microfilm and as digital images.

For a seller, the clerk is the last stop on a sale. The deed is signed, the transfer tax is paid, and recording puts the buyer's ownership on the public record. Most of the paperwork rides along with the closing agent, but knowing the rules helps when a deed is signed outside a title office.

What formatting rules does the Fayette County Clerk enforce on deeds?

The Kentucky County Clerks Association adopted the Property Records Industry Association standards for real estate documents on January 1, 2020, and Fayette applies them. A document that breaks the rules can be turned away at the desk, so check the layout before the signing appointment.

  • Paper: 20 lb white stock with no watermarks, 8.5 by 11 inches preferred and 8.5 by 14 accepted, printed on one side only.
  • Margins: leave 3 inches blank at the top of page one for the recorder's stamp, and 1 inch elsewhere.
  • Text: 10-point Times New Roman or similar, no more than nine lines per inch, in black ink with dark blue signatures.
  • No staples or binding, no colored highlighter marks and no embossed seals unless inked.

The clerk's recording list is wide. It covers deeds, quitclaim deeds, easements, powers of attorney, land contracts, affidavits of descent or heirship, mortgages, releases, lis pendens notices, judgment and mechanic's liens, and wills. A corrective deed or an affidavit of heirship goes through the same desk.

How does a deed reach the Fayette County Clerk?

Documents can be brought to the recording desk in person from 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. on weekdays, and three other routes are open.

  • E-recording: the office accepts submissions through CSC, ePN, Simplifile and Hopdox, the channels title companies already use.
  • Mail or courier: send documents by US Mail, UPS or FedEx to Fayette County Clerk, 162 E. Main Street, Room 132, Lexington, KY 40507.
  • Drop box: a box in the Helix Garage, near the second-floor entrance to the clerk's office and to the right of the yellow garage fee kiosk, takes envelopes from 7:30 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. Monday through Friday. The last pickup of the day is at 4:00 p.m., and documents must be sealed in envelopes.

Veterans can have a DD-214 discharge recorded at the clerk's office at no charge and receive a copy without a fee. Those records are closed to the public, so copies require photo identification and, in some cases, a birth certificate.

What does recording a deed cost in Fayette County?

State law sets the recording fee: $33 buys a deed of up to five pages. KRS 64.012, in the version that took effect July 15, 2026, lists the rest of the schedule, and the clerk adds its own copy charges. Ask the clerk's land records staff for the current fee sheet before closing.

Mail requests add $1.00 for postage and handling, and mailing a plat copy commonly costs $2.00. The statute also lets the clerk collect a $10 reimbursement for permanent record storage on deeds, plats and mortgages. Cash, credit cards or checks are accepted at the window for copy fees.

How does Kentucky's transfer tax work on a Fayette County sale?

The levy falls on the grantor and counts every $500 of declared value, rounding a partial block up. KRS 142.050 requires the county clerk to compute the tax and collect it before accepting the deed for recording. On a sale, value means the full price including liens; on a gift, the estimated open-market price.

Take $293,500, the Census median for owner-occupied homes here: that is 587 blocks of $500, so the tax is $293.50. A $250,000 sale produces $250.00. From each collection the clerk retains 5 percent, then remits the balance quarterly to the county treasurer for the general fund.

Exempt transfers include those between spouses or ex-spouses in a divorce, parent to child or grandparent to grandchild for nominal consideration, foreclosure and deed-in-lieu transfers, delinquent tax sales, partitions, and deeds that only confirm or fix an earlier one. A clerk who records a taxable deed without collecting the tax is fined $50 per offense.

Use fayettedeeds.com, the clerk's online portal. Land records from 1970 to the present can be searched, viewed and printed there, and many earlier records sit in the non-indexed documents section. All plats have been digitized. Since January 3, 2022, the clerk has indexed documents exactly as written on the document instead of using its older abbreviation list, so searching a few spelling variations is wise.

The clerk's free Recording Notification Service emails you when a document is recorded against a registered name or address, with room for 10 items per email address. It is sometimes called a fraud alert, and the clerk cautions that it gives no guarantee of catching every filing.

  • Check the portal now and then for anything recorded in your name or against your property.
  • Look often at vacant property to be sure no one is occupying it unlawfully.
  • Give the PVA and the sheriff your correct mailing address so tax bills and notices reach you.
  • If fraud is suspected, call the Lexington Police Department at 859-258-3600 and a lawyer. The clerk cannot remove a recorded document without a court order.

The same office collects delinquent real property taxes once the sheriff passes them on after April 15, takes only cash, money order or cashier's or certified check, and searches delinquent bills on fayettedeeds.com. The 2026 delinquent tax sale was held on July 24 at 11:00 a.m.

What should a seller in Fayette County know about the local market?

Fayette County is a consolidated city-county government, so one office, the clerk, serves all of Lexington's recording needs. The Census Bureau counts 139,715 households averaging 2.23 people, and 79.8 percent of residents were in the same house a year earlier. Monthly owner costs have a median of $1,636 with a mortgage and $599 without, and renters pay a median of $1,164.

Record it with the Fayette County Clerk's Land Records department, Room 132 at 162 East Main Street in Lexington. You can walk it in, mail it, use the Helix Garage drop box or e-record through an approved vendor.

What time does the Fayette County Clerk stop recording documents?

Recording stops at 4:00 p.m. on weekdays, even though the office answers copy requests and inquiries until 4:30 p.m. The drop box's last pickup is also 4:00 p.m.

What transfer tax applies to a Fayette County sale?

The seller as grantor pays $0.50 for every $500 of value. A $293,500 sale produces a $293.50 tax, which the clerk collects before recording.

Yes. Search fayettedeeds.com for land records from 1970 to the present, plus many older records in the non-indexed section. Plats are all online, and certified marriage records can be ordered there.

Yes, once the sheriff transfers a delinquent bill after April 15. Pay the clerk in full by cash, money order or cashier's or certified check. The County Attorney, at 859-254-4941, arranges payment plans.

The Clerk's checklist asks that a deed claiming exemption name the statute behind it.

What makes the Clerk turn a deed away?

Papers that miss the formatting or content checklist are returned at the counter. The checklist borrows the PRIA national layout standards that the Kentucky County Clerks Association adopted for filings from 2020 onward.

  • White letter-size paper, printed one side, with no staples, binding, embossed seals or highlighter.
  • Ten-point Times New Roman or a close match, black ink, and a three-inch blank band atop page one.
  • A preparation statement signed by whoever prepared the document. A "Drafted by" line does not count.
  • Full addresses for both parties, and a mailing address for future tax bills.
  • A legal description, the deed or will book and page of the seller's title, and a stated fair market value.
  • A notary block showing the notary's ID number and naming grantor and grantee.
  • An original or certified copy with the right fee in a signed check.

If the seller is a corporation, LLC or partnership, the Secretary of State must have the entity on file before the clerk will take its deed. Settle that point a week or two before the closing date.

How are mortgage payoffs recorded in Jefferson County?

Your lender files a release at $46 after the payoff clears. When a deed and a release travel together, the posted price for the pair is $96.

The Clerk's guidance reminds filers that a mortgage is recorded where the land sits, per KRS 382.110, and that it binds third parties from the moment it is acknowledged and recorded under KRS 382.080. The release must cite the book and page of the mortgage it wipes out, and the closing agent usually gets that from the title search.

Request a payoff letter that stays good through the closing date. Afterward, ask the title company when the release went out. A mortgage that stays open on the Jefferson County record can complicate the next owner's loan.

How does unpaid property tax reach the Clerk?

At the close of business on April 15, any current-year bill still open leaves the Sheriff and lands with the Clerk as a certificate of delinquency. By then the Sheriff's schedule has added a 10 percent penalty and a 10 percent add-on fee, and the Clerk's side starts adding interest at 1 percent per month.

The County Attorney's tax page puts the combined extra cost near 40 percent once a certificate exists, and says certificates accrue interest at 12 percent a year. Each summer the Clerk holds a lien sale, and bills that fail to sell stay open for purchase all year. A buyer of a certificate can pile its own charges on top.

If nobody has bought the certificate, pay the Clerk at 527 W. Jefferson St., Room 100. Mailed payments must be certified or cashier's checks or money orders, because the office rejects personal checks and phone payments. A bill placed on a County Attorney payment plan cannot be sold at the sale.

Sellers should order a payoff figure before the listing goes live. Then the buyer's title company can settle it out of the proceeds.

What do sellers need to know about Jefferson County itself?

Kentucky's largest county covers 380.8 square miles of land along the Ohio River, and since the 2003 merger its lines match those of Louisville, the county seat. Jeffersontown, St. Matthews, Middletown and dozens of smaller cities still keep their own governments inside Louisville Metro.

Public schools come from Jefferson County Public Schools and the Anchorage Independent district, which stops at eighth grade. Census QuickFacts reports:

  • 795,222 residents in the 2025 estimate, up 1.6 percent from the April 2020 base.
  • 366,702 housing units counted in 2025.
  • 62.1 percent of households own their home (2020 to 2024).
  • $248,400 as the typical owned-home value.
  • $1,149 as median gross rent.
  • $69,866 as median household income.
  • 3,001 building permits issued during 2025.

The PVA's count of 83 taxing jurisdictions includes about 60,000 properties in the smaller home rule cities, many of which send their own bill. Recording works the same across all of them, but a seller in a small city should check for a city tax balance before closing.

More questions about Jefferson County, KY County Clerk

Which office takes a deed for a house in Louisville?

The Jefferson County Clerk's Legal Records Division, in the Deed Room at Metro Hall, 527 W. Jefferson St., Room 204. Phone 502-574-6220. The closing agent normally files for the buyer, and the office also takes electronic filings.

What will I pay to put a deed on record?

The posted rate is $50 for a deed and $96 when a release is filed with it. Mailed instruments add $1 for postage from September 1, 2026, and the separate transfer tax runs 50 cents per $500 of value.

Is the transfer tax charged to me or to the buyer?

Charged to you as grantor. KRS 142.050 imposes it on the seller named in the deed. Transfers such as those between spouses or through foreclosure are exempt when the deed cites the exemption.

Why would the Clerk reject my paperwork?

Typical causes are a missing preparation statement, no source of title, no stated market value, no tax-bill mailing address, a weak notary block or the wrong fee. An LLC seller also has to be registered with the Secretary of State first.

I owe back tax on the house. Where do I start?

Ask the Sheriff for any current-year balance before April 15, and the Clerk for older certificates afterward. Get both figures in writing before listing so the title company can pay them at closing. The County Attorney's Tax Division handles payment plans.

Henderson County by the numbers

What does the Henderson County Clerk do for a home seller?

The clerk's land records office records and indexes the paper that moves title: deeds, land contracts, mortgages, liens, releases, plats and powers of attorney. It sits in the Henderson County Courthouse, 20 N Main Street, Suite 206, Henderson, KY 42420, on the Ohio River side of western Kentucky.

The county describes three ways to file. You can bring documents in during office hours, send them by mail, or use an eRecording vendor. The county lists three vendors: Simplifile, CSC and ePN, and each charges the submitter its own fee. Wills, will disclaimers, state and federal tax liens and releases, and mobile home conversion affidavits cannot go through eRecording and need to be filed another way.

After recording, originals come back by mail on the next business day, or you can collect them. The office's records reach back to 1786 and sit in record books, on microfilm, as digital images and online. A subscription service called TitleSearcher offers monthly or pay-as-you-go access to view and print recorded documents, which is useful when a seller needs a copy of an old deed or release.

How much does it cost to record documents in Henderson County?

A standard deed costs $50 to record, and a mortgage costs $80, under the Henderson County Clerk's fee schedule that took effect July 15, 2026. Each fee covers the first five pages, and each extra page is $3. Mortgages and a few other instruments include 30 pages.

Selected Henderson County Clerk recording fees (source: clerk fee schedule effective July 15, 2026)
DocumentFee
Deed$50.00
Corrected deed$46.00
Easement$50.00
Deed release$46.00
Mortgage (30 pages included)$80.00
Mortgage release$46.00
Power of attorney$50.00
Encumbrance such as a lis pendens or judgment lien$46.00
Certified copy$5.00
Copies made in the office$0.50 per page

Extra notations that reference another recorded instrument add $4 per reference. Plain copies sent by mail, email or fax run a flat $2 plus 50 cents a page, with a minimum charge of $2.50.

What transfer tax does the Henderson County Clerk collect on a deed?

Henderson County's transfer tax page restates KRS 142.050 in six lines, and the practical rule is simple: no tax, no recording. The seller, called the grantor, owes half a dollar for each $500 of value or part of $500, and the clerk takes it at the counter.

For an ordinary sale, value is the full price, liens included. For a gift or token-price deed, it is the figure the open market would pay. The Census median home value for the county is $171,900, which divides into 344 units and a tax of $172. A $250,000 sale carries $250.

  • The tax is paid once per transaction, in the county where the deed must be recorded.
  • The clerk retains 5 percent and remits the rest to the county treasurer every quarter.
  • Foreclosure deeds, divorce transfers between spouses and deeds that merely correct an earlier one owe nothing.

What does a Henderson County deed need before the clerk accepts it?

Two items catch sellers off guard: a sworn statement of consideration and an in-care-of tax mailing address. The clerk's pages cite KRS 382.135 for both.

Both sides sign the consideration certificate before a notary, whether in person or through an agent. On a sale it confirms that the deed shows the full price. On a gift it says so and gives an estimated fair cash value. A swap states each property's fair cash value in the deed. When property passes at death, the personal representative files an affidavit before the estate closes.

The exceptions are few: utility easements, divorce-court transfers, rights of way for agencies, cemetery lots, same-party correction deeds and deeds to a local airport board. The airport deed skips the certificate but still owes transfer tax.

Land contracts follow their own rule. The contract names both parties, gives the buyer's mailing address, a legal description, the source of title and a preparation statement, and a notary witnesses both signatures. The tax is collected when the deed follows, not on the contract.

What else does the Henderson County Clerk record besides deeds?

The fee schedule reads like an index of local paperwork, and several items touch a sale or an estate.

  • Wills, $47 flat as of July 15, 2026, and will disclaimers or renunciations, $46 each.
  • Affidavits of descent, $50, used when property passes by inheritance.
  • Plats up to 24 by 36 inches, $50, and their revocation, $50.
  • Fixture filings, $96, and fixture releases, which carry no fee.
  • Name changes, $46 flat, and articles of incorporation or organization, $46.
  • Marriage licenses, $60, and notary bonds, $19.

Veterans' discharge papers are recorded at no charge. Certified copies run $5 with an extra 50 cents per page after the third.

Which liens does the Henderson County Clerk record?

The clerk's encumbrance book holds the claims a title search will find. Knowing the list helps a seller anticipate what must be cleared.

  • Lis pendens and judgment liens, $46 to record and $46 to release.
  • Federal tax liens, $46, and their releases, $46.
  • State tax liens and in-state child support liens, a flat $5 each.
  • Mechanic's liens, $46, plus a $60 charge to record a bond that releases one.
  • Assignments of a certificate of delinquency, $30, which come up when an investor buys an unpaid tax bill.

Each lien that shows up in a title search needs a recorded release, and the payoff comes from you or from the closing proceeds.

How do unpaid Henderson County property taxes reach the clerk?

The sheriff collects the bill first, then hands uncollected bills to the clerk, where interest of 1 percent per month plus penalties accrue until paid. The county attorney's FAQ states that a bill turns delinquent on January 1 following its due date.

You can settle a delinquent bill in person at the courthouse or mail a personal check, cashier's check, money order or certified check to Henderson County Clerk, 20 N Main Street, 2nd Floor Offices, Henderson, Kentucky 42420. Cards are accepted for a small extra fee, and the number for details is 270-827-5753. At the tax sale, any qualified individual or company can buy the bill, and the buyer then has 50 days to notify the owner.

The buyer may sue to foreclose one year after the certificate is created. Because the property carries a lien until the bill is paid in full, a seller who sees an unpaid year in the file should resolve it before a buyer's title company does.

Anyone who buys the bill must follow KRS 134.490, KRS 134.546 and the rest of Chapter 134. A seller who pays such a buyer can get a copy of the recorded release from the clerk for a small fee at Suite 206 of the courthouse, which is worth keeping for the title company.

More questions about Henderson County, KY County Clerk

What is the recording fee for a deed in Henderson County, KY?

$50 for a standard deed, including the first five pages, under the fee schedule effective July 15, 2026. Each additional page is $3.

Can I record a Henderson County deed electronically?

Yes. The office accepts most documents through Simplifile, CSC or ePN. Wills, tax liens and mobile home conversion affidavits are excluded, and the vendors add their own fee.

Who pays the real estate transfer tax in Henderson County?

The grantor, meaning the seller. The tax is fifty cents per $500 of value, and the clerk collects it before recording the deed.

Do I need a notarized consideration certificate in Henderson County?

Yes, for nearly every deed. Both parties sign a sworn, notarized statement of the true consideration or, for a gift, the estimated fair cash value.

How soon do I get my recorded deed back?

Recorded documents are mailed back on the next business day, or you can pick up the original at the clerk's office.
